prompt: Write 10 distinct short extracts of Larkmere Mutual's official guidance, procedures or policy wording about: waiting for the loss adjuster. Two to four sentences each, in the society's own formal voice. Use type "fact". Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"fact","content":"If we appoint a loss adjuster, you must wait for their visit before carrying out permanent repairs, unless urgent action is needed to make the home safe or prevent further damage. We may ask you to preserve any damaged items and keep them available for inspection. Temporary protective measures are allowed where they are reasonably necessary."},{"type":"fact","content":"Please do not dispose of damaged property until we or our loss adjuster have had the opportunity to inspect it. Photographs, receipts and any contractor quotations should be retained for our review. Where items must be discarded for safety reasons, please keep a clear record of what was removed."},{"type":"fact","content":"If a loss adjuster is instructed, they will contact you to arrange an appointment. You should be ready to provide access to the affected rooms, loft, outbuildings and any other areas relevant to the claim. Delays in arranging access may slow our assessment and settlement of the claim."},{"type":"fact","content":"You should continue to take reasonable steps to prevent further loss while waiting for the loss adjuster. This may include turning off water, boarding broken openings or moving undamaged possessions to a dry place. Such steps do not amount to acceptance of liability by us."},{"type":"fact","content":"Do not instruct major repair work until the loss adjuster has inspected the damage and we have confirmed the next steps. If you need emergency repairs to make the property secure, please keep the work to what is strictly necessary. Any wider reinstatement should wait for our authorisation."},{"type":"fact","content":"The loss adjuster will usually record the cause, extent and likely cost of the damage. You must provide honest and complete information and answer any reasonable questions they ask. If further specialist reports are needed, we may defer settlement until those reports are received."},{"type":"fact","content":"Where there is a risk of mould, contamination or structural instability, you should wait for guidance from the loss adjuster before disturbing the affected area further. We may permit limited drying, cleaning or stabilisation where this is necessary to reduce the loss. Any such work should be proportionate and documented."},{"type":"fact","content":"If we agree that you may proceed before the loss adjuster attends, that agreement will be limited to the specific work described. It does not mean that all costs will be accepted. You remain responsible for ensuring the work is reasonable and properly evidenced."},{"type":"fact","content":"You must tell us promptly if the loss adjuster cannot gain access on the arranged date. We may need to reschedule and, where repeated delays occur, we may ask you to contact us to explain the reason. Failure to cooperate may affect the handling of the claim."},{"type":"fact","content":"Once the loss adjuster has inspected the damage, they may ask for further information before we decide the claim. Please keep any quotations, invoices and correspondence until the claim is fully resolved. Waiting for inspection and further instructions helps us assess the loss fairly and accurately."}]}
